tpText.AM-CCF-1:TP1: Confirm the use of CSO‑approved encryption algorithms for sensitive media in transit (e.g., AES 128-bit and above, Triple DES, RSA 2048 and above, SHA-2 and SHA-3).
tpText.AM-CCF-1:TP2: Inquire with the control owner and the IR team to confirm that mechanisms exist to report, escalate, and deactivate lost, stolen, or missing devices.
tpText.AM-CCF-1:TP3: Verify, through incident logs, deactivation requests, or ticketing records, that affected devices (e.g., laptops, mobile phones, tablets, USB drives, or any device storing IDs or passwords) were electronically deactivated immediately as per the GSK Standard.
tpText.CM-CCF-14:TP1: Extract a list of all system and service accounts (non-user accounts) from selected systems. Verify that such accounts have been removed or disabled.
tpText.CM-CCF-14:TP2: Ensure periodic assessments for system and service accounts are completed.
tpText.CM-CCF-14:TP3: Approved networking ports and protocols follow production network standards.
tpText.CM-CCF-14:TP4: Disable or restrict all unnecessary programs, functions, ports, protocols, and services to minimize attack vector. Protocols not required should be turned off; always use secure versions.
tpText.CM-CCF-14:TP5: For cloud services, standardized secure protocols are used for management, with documentation on interoperability and portability provided. Where there is a deviation, ensure to raise an Issue.
tpText.CM-CCF-17:TP2: Confirm that servers must not host multiple unrelated roles or responsibilities.
tpText.IM-CCF-1:TP1: RACI matrix of the SailPoint groups (or similar tool) are defined and documented in Approved SAP document.
tpText.IM-CCF-1:TP2: All Privilege accounts and Service/Functional accounts are secured using the CyberArk and documented in System Access Plan.
tpText.SA-CCF-25:TP1: Verify that a Web Application Firewall (WAF) is configured and actively monitors and blocks web‑based attacks for all public‑facing applications.
tpText.SA-CCF-25:TP2: Confirm that all end‑user and web traffic routes through a proxy server and that any bypass attempts are blocked. Also ensure that the proxy server is integrated with GSK directory services and handles authentication for both authorized and unauthorized access attempts.
tpText.SA-CCF-25:TP3: Review network access request documentation to ensure approved IPs, ports, services, and the defined access purpose are properly documented.
tpText.SA-CCF-25:TP4: For SaaS applications, confirm the availability and review of SOC 2 Type II or penetration testing reports to validate security controls.
tpText.SA-CCF-27:TP1: Review network topology diagrams to confirm a dedicated DMZ segment exists and ensure internal resources are only accessed via approved firewall rules.
tpText.SA-CCF-27:TP2: Ensure that the firewall port exception request is raised whenever application uses custom ports.
tpText.SA-CCF-27:TP3: Check that critical internal systems are not exposed via public IPs.
tpText.SA-CCF-6:TP1: Review network architecture diagrams, firewall rules, and system placements to ensure appropriate segmentation, e.g., public systems in an external DMZ and critical shared services in an internal DMZ.
tpText.SA-CCF-6:TP2: For SaaS applications, confirm the availability and review of SOC2 Type II report.
tpText.SD-CCF-11:TP1: Verify the segregation of production and non-production environments in the CMDB (ServiceNow).
tpText.SD-CCF-11:TP2: Verify the segregation of environments from POM/Design Specification/System Design document/Architecture.
tpText.SD-CCF-11:TP3: Verify the segregation of environments for SaaS products from SOC 2 Type II/TPRM reports.
tpText.SM-CCF-11:TP1: Verify that all system components forward logs to the centralized log management solution using the approved organizational log format.
tpText.SM-CCF-11:TP2: Confirm that logging is enabled for all required application and infrastructure event categories demonstrating full coverage.
tpText.SM-CCF-11:TP3: Validate that periodic stakeholder reviews of logged event types are documented and result in updates to log‑management procedures (e.g., POM) and check that updated procedures reflect enhancements identified during reviews and are communicated to relevant product and operational teams.

tpText.REG-SOX-1:TP4: There is sufficient evidence of review performed for each change implemented to production during the period under review
tpText.REG-SOX-1:TP5: Ensure all follow up actions are appropriately actioned and evidence is retained
tpText.REG-SOX-1:TP6: Ensure overall review has been signed off by reviewer
tpText.REG-SOX-2:TP1: Obtain listing of users who have access to schedule and change batch jobs and batch processes
tpText.REG-SOX-2:TP2: Based on users job role, determine if access is appropriate and commensurate with job responsibilities
tpText.REG-SOX-3:TP1: Obtain a listing of new jobs and tie back to approved change ticket
tpText.REG-SOX-4:TP1: Obtain a log of all in scope jobs from application
tpText.REG-SOX-4:TP2: Select a sample of failures and compare to SLA to identify if they required investigation and follow up
tpText.REG-SOX-4:TP3: For failures required investigation, ensure ticket was raised and investigation was performed in a timely manner.
tpText.REG-SOX-5:TP1: For any changes to the report during the year, ensure report was subject to UAT testing by the business (specifically for completeness and accuracy)
tpText.SA-CCF-12:TP1: If the application is internet‑facing, ensure that the VPN is enabled and documented in the approved DTMS documentation.
tpText.SA-CCF-12:TP2: Disable remote access where it is not required, and ensure that privileged administrative functions are not executed without a GSK‑approved VPN connection.
tpText.SA-CCF-14:TP1: Check encryption status by verifying that AES‑256 disk/file encryption is enabled on all systems and attempting to read data without decryption keys.
tpText.SA-CCF-14:TP3: Test data classification and DLP implementation.
tpText.SA-CCF-14:TP4: Validate KMS controls by documenting RBAC permissions, MFA enforcement, and confirming that keys cannot be exported.
tpText.SA-CCF-15:TP1: Verify that sessions terminate after a defined period of inactivity and require re-authentication after session termination.
tpText.SA-CCF-15:TP2: Validate authentication and session management rules to confirm that the account lock out feature triggers after 9 failed login attempts within 15 minutes.
tpText.SA-CCF-15:TP3: Verify that locked accounts are re‑enabled only through authorized and approved administrative processes.
tpText.SA-CCF-20:TP1: Validate the architecture diagram to confirm that only private network paths are used and that traffic does not traverse any public endpoints.
tpText.SA-CCF-20:TP2: Validate cloud console screenshots showing private endpoints/private IP communication.
tpText.SA-CCF-20:TP3: Review ACL configuration and SAP documentation to confirm that no unauthorized access is allowed.
tpText.SA-CCF-20:TP4: For SaaS applications, review the vendor’s SOC 2 Type II or platform/architecture documentation confirming network isolation.
tpText.SA-CCF-3:TP1: Verify use of only CSO-approved cryptographic algorithms.
tpText.SA-CCF-3:TP2: Verify that cryptographic algorithms and key‑usage extensions are applied only for their designated cryptographic services and intended purposes.
tpText.SA-CCF-3:TP3: Validate that key and certificate lifecycle processes are in place, ensuring that only CSO‑approved Certificate Authorities (CAs) issue certificates and that all requests are authenticated and validated.
tpText.SA-CCF-3:TP4: Verify that root certificates and master keys are securely stored offline in controlled environments (e.g., encrypted, HSM‑protected), with strict access controls, logging, rotation, backups, and continuous monitoring.
tpText.SA-CCF-31:TP1: Verify encrypted migration protocols by checking migration tool settings to ensure TLS/SSH are enforced and no plaintext protocol is enabled.
tpText.SA-CCF-31:TP2: Confirm encrypted hypervisor migration by validating that VMware vMotion Encryption or Hyper‑V Encrypted Live Migration is set to required/enabled.
tpText.SA-CCF-31:TP3: Validate secure network paths by reviewing network routing to ensure all migration traffic flows through VPN/IPsec tunnels or private peering only.
tpText.SA-CCF-31:TP4: Check certificate and cipher strength by inspecting TLS configurations to ensure strong ciphers are enabled and weak/legacy ciphers are disabled.
tpText.SA-CCF-4:TP1: Confirm encrypted hypervisor migration by validating that VMware vMotion Encryption or Hyper‑V Encrypted Live Migration is set to required/enabled.
tpText.SA-CCF-5:TP1: Verify the GSK time synchronization configuration screenshot.
tpText.SA-CCF-5:TP2: For SaaS product, verify the SOC 2 Type II report for time synchronization details.
tpText.SA-CCF-8:TP1: Verify that all messaging technologies in scope use approved secure messaging utilities and encrypted transmission protocols.
tpText.SA-CCF-8:TP2: Confirm that message integrity, anti‑tampering mechanisms, and protections against unauthorized modification are enabled and functioning.
tpText.SA-CCF-8:TP3: Validate that system‑to‑system and middleware communication paths enforce authentication and prevent unauthorized access or message injection.
tpText.SA-CCF-8:TP4: Review configuration artifacts to ensure that transport‑layer security controls meet organizational standards for all channels handling sensitive data.
tpText.SA-DCJ-3:TP1: Diagrams showing encrypted data flows between systems, including VPN tunnels, secure APIs, and encryption gateways.
tpText.SA-DCJ-3:TP2: Up to date and approved Cryptographic Policy/procedure for DCJ systems.
tpText.SA-DCJ-3:TP3: System configuration files showing encryption settings (e.g., OpenSSL configurations, database encryption settings).
tpText.SA-DCJ-3:TP4: Test cases and results verifying data encryption during transit and at rest (e.g., using tools like Wireshark to verify TLS traffic encryption).
tpText.SA-DCJ-3:TP5: Logs from encryption-related events (e.g., TLS handshake logs, key access logs.
tpText.SA-OT-14:TP1: Verify in the device network settings that OT wireless is the only network enabled.
tpText.SA-OT-16:TP1: Verify that the OT solutions matches the Enabling Services definition. Verify that the enabling service specifications have been documented. Verify that CSRB has approved the enabling service for use in OT.
tpText.SA-OT-17:TP1: Verify that OT system architecture is documented and segmentation applied.
tpText.SA-OT-17:TP2: Verify that OT security Architects have completed the review with no critical contingencies
tpText.SA-OT-19:TP1: Verify traffic flows between OT network zones have been identified and confirmed as required and aligned with the least privilege principle.
tpText.SA-OT-19:TP2: Verify all the traffic flow go is routed through a security engine and that policies only allow documented traffic flows.
tpText.SA-OT-19:TP3: Verify that OT security Architects consultation has not identified critical findings or OT CSRB has approved with no critical contingencies.
tpText.SA-OT-20:TP1: Verify that OT assets are permanently attached to their designated OT network zone and are not connected to other zones.
tpText.SA-OT-20:TP2: Verify that non OT assets are not attached to OT network zones.
tpText.SA-OT-22:TP1: Verify using the approved network diagram that no endpoint is configured to bridge network zones.
tpText.SA-OT-22:TP2: Verify that endpoints do not have multiple active network interfaces that connect different network zones at the same time.
tpText.SA-OT-23:TP1: Verify that the software installed on the OT asset is not general purpose IT software.
tpText.SA-OT-23:TP2: Verify that the OT asset does not have access to general purpose IT services (e.g. public Internet, corporate email, O365 etc).
tpText.SA-OT-3:TP1: Verify that the security configuration supports the operational and maintenance activities required for the OT asset and that no security configuration setting prevents the OT asset from performing its required operational or maintenance activities.
tpText.SA-OT-4:TP1: Verify that removable media ports on the OT asset are disabled when not in use using physical or logical controls.
tpText.SA-OT-7:TP1: Verify protocol utilized for RF communications and confirm that documentation exists for the selected standard protocol and approval from OT CSRB has been obtained for the use of any proprietary protocol.
tpText.SA-OT-7:TP2: Verify which RF pairing method is used and confirm that only authorised devices can join the RF network.
tpText.SA-OT-7:TP3: Validate default join keys/credentials are changed and do not utilize default values.
tpText.SA-OT-9:TP1: Verify that remote connections into the OT Asset are by design aligned to the interzone communication requirements described in the Operational Technology Security Reference Architecture (VQD-REF-024763).
tpText.SD-CCF-10:TP1: Obtain and review acceptance testing evidences and ensure:
tpText.SD-CCF-10:TP2: It is reviewed and approved by relevant stakeholders in accordance with GxP/Standard Track WI (WI10/11)
tpText.SD-CCF-10:TP3: All planned acceptance testing scenarios/cases have been completed and recorded.
tpText.SD-CCF-10:TP6: To what extent, if any, the vendor testing is being relied on, instead of performing tests by GSK.
tpText.SD-CCF-12:TP1: Ensure that production data, critical sensitive information and restrictive/sensitive PI are not used for testing or development. Ensure where possible, synthetic test data is used, and production data used for testing is anonymized, protected, and removed when no longer needed. Test data is removed immediately after testing, and all test data and accounts are eliminated from system components before the system goes into production. Ensure testing information is documented and approved (e.g. POM, GPOM, testing documentation) If providing any documentation as evidence provide the document name, location and VQD identifier if applicable.
tpText.SD-CCF-13:TP1: Verify each change through the corresponding Change Request ticket.
tpText.SD-CCF-13:TP2: For SaaS applications, refer to the TPRM.
tpText.SD-CCF-18:TP1: For SaaS Vendor: - SOC 2 Type II Certification or Equivalent evidence such as, Secure code testing, SAST or DAST scanning or Pentest (if applicable, covering AI threats) conducted based on OWASP framework.
tpText.SD-CCF-18:TP2: On Prem / GSK Cloud : conduct the SAST or DAST scan where applicable, PenTest report from AST team where applicable.
tpText.SD-CCF-3:TP1: Obtain and review evidence that BU Privacy Contact/Privacy Leader was consulted reg. the privacy risks to determine whether completion of PIA or any other actions were required.
tpText.SD-CCF-3:TP2: Verify that any identified actions (mainly completion of PIA) were completed.
tpText.SD-CCF-3:TP3: In the BAU phase of the Tech product, confirm that any changes to Personal Information processing within the product are assessed for impact on Privacy Risks. Verify if the Privacy SME is consulted when needed, and PIA is updated.
tpText.SD-CCF-4:TP1: Verify a change control for initial release to Production is recorded and approved in ServiceNow.
tpText.SD-CCF-4:TP2: Inquire with the Tech Owner of the system if there were any changes to the Tech product which were not recorded in CMDB (or other approved tool). In case such changes exist, verify rationale for not recording them and the performed change activities to assess the risks connected with not following the standard change management process.
tpText.SD-CCF-5:TP1: Confirm that access to development and production environments is restricted to authorized personnel.
tpText.SD-CCF-5:TP2: Ensure that development, testing, and production environments are properly separated
tpText.SD-CCF-5:TP3: Confirm that developers and migrators are distinct roles, ensuring that the same individual cannot both develop and implement changes in the production environment. This may require a user list /screenshot of the users per environment. Ensure privileged users are accessing environment through privileged accounts.
tpText.SD-CCF-5:TP4: Verify that access restrictions for system changes, including ability to initiate, approve, and implement changes, are as per the approved System Access plan.
tpText.SD-CCF-5:TP5: Verify that the development, testing, and production environments continue to be physically or logically separated and access controlled.
tpText.SD-CCF-6:TP1: Verify access to change (including software, source code, pipelines, development artifacts, container registries, and other system components) is tightly restricted. Verify clear roles and responsibilities are defined, and access are reviewed regularly to reduce the risk of unauthorized or accidental changes—especially in production adn is documented and approved (e.g. POM, GPOM, System Access Plan) Verify that development, test and production environments are separated and access is managed for each environment separately (CMDB or documented (e.g. POM, GPOM, System Access Plan) If any documentation is provided as evidence verify that the correct document name, location and VQD identifier if applicable are also provided in the response.
tpText.SD-DCJ-10:TP1: WAST/PT scan tool report including date of scan, scope of scan, list of vulnerabilities found, status.
tpText.SD-DCJ-10:TP2: Sample Jira ticket for WAST highlight status post re-scan and security approval post re-scan.
tpText.SD-DCJ-10:TP3: Penetration test report including date of the test and resulting findings.
tpText.SD-DCJ-9:TP1: List of code repositories stored in GitHub for the application, including descriptions.
tpText.SD-DCJ-9:TP2: Snapshots of GitHub repositories demonstrating ownership and associated details.
tpText.SD-DCJ-9:TP3: Configuration Items created in ServiceNow for DCJ application that includes repository details.
tpText.SM-CCF-2:TP1: Obtain the documentation that is line with the DTMS-POM/GPOM template.
tpText.SM-CCF-2:TP2: Obtain and review configuration/screenshots from the system (like OS, Kubernetes, etc) that logging is enabled and logs are forwarded to centralized SIEM solution.
tpText.SM-CCF-2:TP3: Obtain and review screenshots of logs generated by application. For SaaS Product- Obtain and review
tpText.SM-CCF-2:TP4: Copy/screenshot of contractual agreement with vendor to ensure binding agreements for logging
tpText.SM-CCF-2:TP5: SOC2 Type2 or ISO 27001 report to demonstrate vendor manages logs per design
tpText.SM-CCF-2:TP6: Screenshots to demonstrate logs are generated as designed and forwarded (where integration is possible with SIEM) For Other Applications- Obtain and review
tpText.SM-CCF-2:TP7: POM/GPOM to demonstrate log management is defined
tpText.SM-CCF-2:TP8: Screenshot/configuration for from the system to ensure logs are enabled and configured to forward to SIEM solution.
tpText.SM-CCF-2:TP9: Screenshots to demonstrate logs are generated as designed and forwarded.
tpText.SM-CCF-3:TP1: Verify documented role definitions and permissions governing who may review, analyse, or report on audit logs.
tpText.SM-CCF-3:TP2: Confirm that log storage locations are secure and that logs from external‑facing technologies flow into a centralized log repository.
tpText.SM-CCF-3:TP3: Validate that access to audit logs is restricted to authorized individuals and that approvals are evidenced through the formal workflow.
tpText.SM-CCF-5:TP1: Validate that privileged and attempted‑privileged actions are fully logged with details such as a user ID, timestamp, and action performed.
tpText.SM-CCF-5:TP2: Confirm that logs include failed privileged authentication or authorization attempts as well as attempted execution of privileged functions.
tpText.SM-CCF-5:TP3: Review evidence showing that logged privileged actions map to corresponding approved change records or service tickets.
tpText.SM-GXP-1:TP2: Confirm that the system generates secure, time-stamped audit trails that are available, convertible, and printable in a human-readable format.
tpText.SM-GXP-1:TP3: Review system configuration settings and sample audit logs to ensure they are formatted correctly and contain the required time stamps and other key event details.
tpText.SM-GXP-1:TP4: Review of Audit Trail Retention and Protection:
tpText.SM-GXP-1:TP5: Verify that audit trails are retained for at least as long as the records' full life cycle and that users cannot disable the logs.
tpText.SM-GXP-1:TP6: Review retention policies and verify that audit logs are protected from unauthorized modification, access, or deletion through proper access controls and encryption mechanisms.
tpText.SM-GXP-1:TP8: Ensure that any modification to critical data is recorded with the reason for the change and that the modification does not obscure previously recorded information.
tpText.SM-GXP-1:TP9: Review sample logs for instances of data modification and confirm that the logs include the reason for changes, ensuring previous entries are preserved.
tpText.SM-GXP-1:TP11: Confirm that privileged activities (e.g., security assessments, testing, and compliance checks) are logged in the system’s event logs or audit trails.
tpText.SM-GXP-1:TP12: Review logs for privileged activity to verify that the details include the user, date/time, and nature of the changes, as well as the classification of the activity (e.g., security assessments, compliance checks).
tpText.SM-GXP-1:TP13: Privileged Operations Logging for Critical Data Stores:
tpText.SM-GXP-1:TP14: Ensure that privileged operations executed against production systems and critical data stores (e.g., regulatory, confidential, proprietary) are logged.
tpText.SM-GXP-1:TP15: Review logs for privileged operations to confirm that all relevant actions on critical data stores are captured, including user identifiers and the specific actions performed.
tpText.SM-GXP-1:TP17: Verify that the Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system is configured to monitor privileged authentication and authorization events for critical data stores.
tpText.SM-GXP-1:TP18: Review SIEM logs and monitoring configurations to confirm that privileged operations are being actively tracked and correlated to prevent potential security incidents.
tpText.SM-GXP-1:TP20: Confirm that logs generated by IT, IoT, and Tech-managed OT devices are timestamped to UTC/GMT.
tpText.SM-GXP-1:TP21: Review sample logs from IT, IoT, and OT devices to ensure that the timestamp is in the UTC/GMT format.
tpText.SM-GXP-1:TP23: Ensure that all privileged operations are traceable to a documented local instruction, change request, service request, or incident.
tpText.SM-GXP-1:TP24: Review records of privileged activities to ensure they are linked to appropriate documentation, such as change requests, service requests, or incident logs.
tpText.TA-CCF-5:TP1: Verification of Secure Coding Training Content:
tpText.TA-CCF-5:TP2: Confirm that the training content covers secure coding practices and guidelines for software development personnel.
tpText.TA-CCF-5:TP3: Review the training curriculum or materials to ensure that it includes topics related to secure coding practices, security vulnerabilities, and secure coding guidelines.
tpText.TA-CCF-5:TP5: Ensure that secure coding training has been assigned to all relevant personnel involved in software development.
tpText.TA-CCF-5:TP6: Review training assignment records, such as training logs or personnel lists, to verify that all software development personnel have been assigned the appropriate training.
tpText.TP-CCF-5:TP1: Verify TPRM report ID is in the TPRM dashboard and is valid Verify the Contract ID and applicable contract repository are documented or the approval page of the contract has been screenshot and uploaded.
tpText.TP-DCJ-1:TP1: Third party, vendor names and TPRM ID snapshot from ServiceNow.
tpText.TP-DCJ-1:TP4: Contract showcasing inclusion of required clauses for DCJ, MSB controls.
tpText.TP-SOX-1:TP1: SOC 1 Type 2 (ISAE 3402) report is received in a timely manner from the vendor
tpText.TP-SOX-1:TP2: The scope, exceptions, recommendations and complimentary controls are reviewed and assessed by the application owner
tpText.TP-SOX-1:TP3: The scope of the SOC report is assessed against the ITGC controls expected to be covered including controls on all three layers (OS,DB and application)
tpText.TP-SOX-1:TP4: Complimentary User Entity Controls (CUECs) operated by GSK are mapped and effective
tpText.TP-SOX-1:TP5: If required the bridging letter is received and reviewed to cover the rest of the financial year.
tpText.VM-CCF-3:TP1: For SaaS Vendor: - SOC 2 Type II Certification or Equivalent evidence such as, Vulnerability Management (VM) policy and evidence that the VM is conducted and issues are addressed based on the scans.
tpText.VM-CCF-3:TP2: On Prem / GSK Cloud : Make sure periodic vulnerability scanning and pentests are conducted and issues are acted upon. In case of no action, exception is documented in SNOW
tpText.VM-CCF-5:TP1: Alert Generation for Logging Failures and Capacity Issues:
tpText.VM-CCF-5:TP2: Verify that alerts are generated for logging mechanism failures and logging storage capacity issues.
tpText.VM-CCF-5:TP3: Simulate logging mechanism failures or storage capacity issues and confirm that alerts are triggered and communicated to the appropriate personnel.
tpText.VM-CCF-5:TP5: Check that change detection mechanisms are in place to detect unauthorized modifications to critical system files, configuration files, log files, or content files.
tpText.VM-CCF-5:TP6: Test the change detection mechanisms by attempting unauthorized modifications to critical files and verifying that alerts are generated and communicated to security personnel.
tpText.VM-CCF-5:TP11: Confirm that alerts regarding logging mechanism failures, storage issues, and unauthorized changes are communicated to the appropriate personnel in a timely manner.
tpText.VM-CCF-5:TP12: Review communication logs (email, tickets, or logs) to ensure that alerts are acknowledged and acted upon promptly.
tpText.VM-CCF-6:TP1: Verify that the vendor penetration‑test report has been reviewed or validated by the GSK AST Team (if applicable).
tpText.VM-CCF-6:TP2: Verify that the SOC 2 Type II report (or equivalent security documentation) has been obtained from the SaaS vendor, confirming the penetration test is conducted periodically.
tpText.VM-CCF-6:TP3: Verify that penetration testing is completed for on‑premises applications and in production environment on a periodic basis or after any significant infrastructure or application upgrade/modification.
tpText.AM-CCF-1:TP4: Confirm the use of CSO‑approved encryption algorithms for sensitive media in transit (e.g., AES 128-bit and above, Triple DES, RSA 2048 and above, SHA-2 and SHA-3).
tpText.AM-CCF-1:TP5: Inquire with the control owner and the IR team to confirm that mechanisms exist to report, escalate, and deactivate lost, stolen, or missing devices.
tpText.AM-CCF-1:TP6: Verify, through incident logs, deactivation requests, or ticketing records, that affected devices (e.g., laptops, mobile phones, tablets, USB drives, or any device storing IDs or passwords) were electronically deactivated immediately as per the GSK Standard.
tpText.CM-CCF-14:TP6: Extract a list of all system and service accounts (non-user accounts) from selected systems. Verify that such accounts have been removed or disabled.
tpText.CM-CCF-14:TP7: Ensure periodic assessments for system and service accounts are completed.
tpText.CM-CCF-14:TP8: Approved networking ports and protocols follow production network standards.
tpText.CM-CCF-14:TP9: Disable or restrict all unnecessary programs, functions, ports, protocols, and services to minimize attack vector. Protocols not required should be turned off; always use secure versions.
tpText.CM-CCF-14:TP10: For cloud services, standardized secure protocols are used for management, with documentation on interoperability and portability provided. Where there is a deviation, ensure to raise an Issue.
tpText.IM-CCF-1:TP3: RACI matrix of the SailPoint groups (or similar tool) are defined and documented in Approved SAP document.
tpText.IM-CCF-1:TP4: All Privilege accounts and Service/Functional accounts are secured using the CyberArk and documented in System Access Plan.
tpText.SA-CCF-25:TP5: Verify that a Web Application Firewall (WAF) is configured and actively monitors and blocks web‑based attacks for all public‑facing applications.
tpText.SA-CCF-25:TP6: Confirm that all end‑user and web traffic routes through a proxy server and that any bypass attempts are blocked. Also ensure that the proxy server is integrated with GSK directory services and handles authentication for both authorized and unauthorized access attempts.
tpText.SA-CCF-25:TP7: Review network access request documentation to ensure approved IPs, ports, services, and the defined access purpose are properly documented.
tpText.SA-CCF-25:TP8: For SaaS applications, confirm the availability and review of SOC 2 Type II or penetration testing reports to validate security controls.
tpText.SA-CCF-27:TP4: Review network topology diagrams to confirm a dedicated DMZ segment exists and ensure internal resources are only accessed via approved firewall rules.
tpText.SA-CCF-27:TP5: Ensure that the firewall port exception request is raised whenever application uses custom ports.
tpText.SA-CCF-27:TP6: Check that critical internal systems are not exposed via public IPs.
tpText.SA-CCF-6:TP3: Review network architecture diagrams, firewall rules, and system placements to ensure appropriate segmentation, e.g., public systems in an external DMZ and critical shared services in an internal DMZ.
tpText.SA-CCF-6:TP4: For SaaS applications, confirm the availability and review of SOC2 Type II report.
tpText.SD-CCF-11:TP4: Verify the segregation of production and non-production environments in the CMDB (ServiceNow).
tpText.SD-CCF-11:TP5: Verify the segregation of environments from POM/Design Specification/System Design document/Architecture.
tpText.SD-CCF-11:TP6: Verify the segregation of environments for SaaS products from SOC 2 Type II/TPRM reports.
tpText.SM-CCF-11:TP4: Verify that all system components forward logs to the centralized log management solution using the approved organizational log format.
tpText.SM-CCF-11:TP5: Confirm that logging is enabled for all required application and infrastructure event categories demonstrating full coverage.
tpText.SM-CCF-11:TP6: Validate that periodic stakeholder reviews of logged event types are documented and result in updates to log‑management procedures (e.g., POM) and check that updated procedures reflect enhancements identified during reviews and are communicated to relevant product and operational teams.
tpText.TP-CCF-6:TP3: Ensure that the TPRM is completed and provide the TPRM ID.
tpText.TP-CCF-6:TP4: Provide the Third-Party Information and Cyber Security Risk Assessment.
tpText.TP-CCF-9:TP4: Verify that the SAP document includes vendor accounts (section 4.2: 'System Access Map') and access reviews (section 4.6: 'Access Review').
tpText.TP-CCF-9:TP5: Verify that GSK SSO implementation is enabled on the system for authentication.
tpText.TP-CCF-9:TP6: Verify that an active TPRM assessment is in place.
tpText.VM-CCF-1:TP5: POM Document with the updated section as below: - Section 6.4, Vulnerability Management actions defined - Vulnerability Management scan report (AST Report)
tpText.VM-CCF-1:TP6: For SaaS : Soc2 Type2 Report along with pentest consultation report from AST team.
tpText.VM-CCF-1:TP7: For GSK Cloud : Evidence that assets used are GSK standard image or Vulnerability Scan Report
tpText.VM-CCF-1:TP8: For On Prem : Evidence that assets used are GSK standard image or Vulnerability Scan Report
tpText.VM-CCF-5:TP7: File Integrity Monitoring for Critical Systems:
tpText.VM-CCF-5:TP8: Verify that integrity monitoring mechanisms are implemented for critical software systems, performing periodic file comparisons of critical files (system, configuration, log, and content files).
tpText.VM-CCF-5:TP9: Review logs or reports from the integrity monitoring tools to confirm that file comparisons are being performed on a regular basis.
tpText.VM-DCJ-6:TP1: Red team exercise reports including date of exercise, scope of exercise, list of vulnerabilities found, status.
tpText.CM-CCF-17:TP3: Confirm that servers must not host multiple unrelated roles or responsibilities.
